Formulation  
A young woman with no prior migraine diagnosis presenting with recurrent throbbing unilateral headaches, associated with nausea, vomiting, and photophobia consistent with migraine. Concurrent psychosocial stress from occupational pressure and significant health anxiety triggered by recent personal loss described (friend’s mother’s brain tumor and death). Protective factors include willingness to seek help and good insight. No immediate neurological concerns identified, but ongoing monitoring is necessary. Stress and anxiety may perpetuate symptom severity.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Migraine headache  
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce headache frequency and severity; return to productive work functioning  
- Clinical Goal(s): Confirm migraine diagnosis; control acute attacks; prevent migraine recurrence  
- Actions (Patient): Maintain headache diary to identify triggers; take prescribed analgesics and anti-inflammatories as advised; rest as needed; monitor symptoms; return if symptoms worsen or new neurological signs occur  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide symptomatic treatment with analgesics (Paracetamol, Co-codamol) and anti-inflammatory agents (Ibuprofen, Naproxen); counsel patient on migraine nature and management; review headache diary and consider prophylactic medication if frequent attacks persist; provide safety netting advice and urgent review criteria  

Secondary Problem: Work-related stress  
- Patient Goal(s): Develop coping strategies to manage occupational stress  
- Clinical Goal(s): Reduce stress impact on mental and physical health  
- Actions (Patient): Attempt stress reduction techniques (not currently doing any); consider increasing physical activity if possible; identify work adjustments if needed  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Explore referral options for stress management or psychological support if stress persists or worsens; discuss lifestyle modification benefits; monitor stress and anxiety regularly  

Tertiary Problem: Health anxiety regarding brain tumor  
- Patient Goal(s): Alleviate excessive health worries; increase understanding of symptoms and prognosis  
- Clinical Goal(s): Provide reassurance; reduce health anxiety  
- Actions (Patient): Engage with education on migraine vs. serious pathology; avoid excessive symptom checking or online searches  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide clear, evidence-based reassurance; discuss natural migraine course; advise on when urgent medical review is needed; offer follow-up to address ongoing anxiety  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Migraine symptoms and triggers, importance of headache diary, distinction between migraine and serious neurological conditions, medication use, red flag symptoms requiring urgent review  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing headache frequency or severity; new neurological symptoms such as weakness, vision changes, speech difficulty; worsening neck pain  
- Coping Strategies: Planned headache diary; medication adherence; consideration of stress management techniques
